name: Leonid Brezhnev
summary: Brezhnev defended developed socialism, public ownership, social guarantees and the Communist Party’s leading role. He pursued arms-control agreements and peaceful coexistence while asserting a right to intervene against threats to socialism and suppressing domestic dissent.

notes:
Downloaded constitutional speech searched across themes. The scanned 1981 report had no extractable text and was not used to assign unsupported energy or technology positions. Constitutional claims and coercive practice are distinguished; all nulls reviewed and no historical extrapolations added. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant. Final wording review left freedom-as-non-domination unknown because the available record addresses a related, narrower or different proposition.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 30 answers taken from it, 25 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (Sonnet) from his own speeches in English translation: Following Lenin's Course (1972 and 1972-75 volumes), Congress reports (24th, 25th, 26th), the 1967 jubilee report and the 1977 constitution report. Texts are in scratchpad/sources/leonid-brezhnev/. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, technology, means. Ecology, technology, and culture are thin: the speeches say little that settles the statements (the 26th Congress scan is garbled in the OCR pages on environment and the Food Programme). Not found as his own words: his stand on religion and the state, media control, elections beyond the party list, and term limits, so those stay null. Words versus record: he claims the republics' right to secede and general disarmament as goals while the record shows neither exercised, so those are 0 at low. Intervention answers rest on his 1968 Warsaw speech and 24th Congress report, where he justifies the Czechoslovak action himself; the Afghanistan invasion is left out because no text of his in these sources explains it.
